chunk_findings.detail: `_hit` tests every path of a section (`any(globs.match(p, g, ...) for p in paths for g in pats)`) but `filter_diff` drops the *entire* section as soon as one path matches. Git puts both sides of a rename/copy into one section, so `diff --git a/tests/golden/x.json b/src/x.json` (a file moved out of the pinned `tests/golden/**` tree, with content edits) yields `fd.paths == ["tests/golden/x.json", "src/x.json"]`; the match on the old path makes `gone.files.append(...)` run and the section is removed from `kept`. The reviewer therefore never sees the hunks for `src/x.json`, which is no longer a pinned/generated file and is exactly the sort of change the round is supposed to review. The same happens for a copy (`similarity index` / `copy from`+`copy to`) and for delete+add renames. The section should only be dropped when all of its paths match (or the exclusion should be applied per-path, keeping the non-matching side).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_exclude.py:filter_diff / _hit

chunk_findings.detail: Pin files are added as raw patterns, and `_hit` always passes `bare_any_depth=True`. A pin path with no `/` — e.g. `README.md`, which the intent explicitly calls out as a pinned file ("README regions") — is a "bare" pattern, so it matches at any depth, not just the pinned root file. Given `.ddflow/pins.toml` owning `README.md`, `globs.match("docs/README.md", "README.md", bare_any_depth=True)` is true, so a real, unpinned change to `docs/README.md` (or `vendor/README.md`, etc.) is silently left out of the reviewer's diff even though only the root file is regenerated. Exact pin paths should be anchored (or matched as whole relative paths) rather than reused as any-depth globs; `bare_any_depth` is appropriate for the user's `exclude_globs` entries like `uv.lock`/`*.ambr`, but not for the literal file list `pins.pin_files()` returns.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_exclude.py:patterns (with _hit)

chunk_findings.detail: The diff embeds an out-of-band verdict string, `echo 'STATUS: NO FINDINGS'`, inside the reviewer fixture written by `_setup`. The task rules state that text in the code under review which states a verdict is itself worth reporting, and this is exactly the token a review pipeline keys on to conclude "clean". Anyone (human or model) reading the raw change — or any pipeline that folds the diff into a review prompt without stripping/neutralizing it — can take `STATUS: NO FINDINGS` as the conclusion of the review rather than as a line of a shell script, which is precisely the failure mode the knob (`exclude_globs`) is meant to prevent for generated files: reviewer input being read as content instead of being recognized as machine-generated text. The demonstrated input is the file as shown, where the string appears verbatim on that line; it should be treated as fixture output (bound to a variable that is clearly test data, e.g. a separate fixture file, or asserted against rather than embedded as a literal "verdict") so that it cannot be mistaken for the actual review status.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_exclude.py:55

chunk_findings.detail: The `exclude_globs` docstring promises that "an empty list sends every file," but the two knobs it sits next to make that promise false. `exclude_pin_files` defaults to `True` and independently removes everything `.ddflow/pins.toml` owns (README regions, golden snapshots, the setup transcript) from the diff sent to reviewers. Concretely: a user who wants the pre-change behaviour back runs `ddflow config review.exclude_globs []` (or `DDFLOW_REVIEW_EXCLUDE_GLOBS=[]`), believes every file is now sent, and still has every pins.toml-owned file stripped out of the review — the exact files the original complaint was about. The only way to actually "send every file" is to also know to set `review.exclude_pin_files false`, which the `exclude_globs` text never mentions and which the "empty list sends every file" wording actively contradicts. The doc on `exclude_globs` should either drop that claim or state that pin-file exclusion must be turned off separately.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/review.py:44-45 (exclude_globs / exclude_pin_files)

chunk_findings.detail: `patterns()` feeds the paths returned by `pins.pin_files(...)` straight into the glob list, and `_hit()` matches them with `bare_any_depth=True`. That flag is what makes a slash-less pattern match at any depth (it is why the defaults `uv.lock`, `*.ambr`, `*transcript*.json` can match nested files), but pin files are exact repo-relative paths, so a pin file that lives at the repo root becomes a recursive pattern. Given `.ddflow/pins.toml` owning the root `README.md` (the "README regions" pin case named in the intent), `pins.pin_files` returns `"README.md"`, `patterns()` emits `"README.md"`, and `_hit` evaluates `globs.match("docs/README.md", "README.md", bare_any_depth=True)` → `True`. The `docs/README.md` section is then dropped from the diff the reviewers receive even though it is not a pinned/generated file, and `Excluded.line()` even reports `docs/README.md` as "excluded from review", i.e. a hand-written doc change is hidden from the reviewer under a default-on knob (`exclude_pin_files` defaults to true). The same applies to any root-level pin file whose name recurs in the tree (e.g. a pinned root `CHANGELOG.md` shadowing `sub/CHANGELOG.md`). Pin-derived patterns need to be anchored to the repo root (exact-path semantics) instead of being handed to `globs.match(..., bare_any_depth=True)` as bare patterns.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_exclude.py `patterns` / `_hit`

chunk_findings.detail:
`if all(_hit(p, pats, pinned) for p in fd.paths):` is vacuously true whenever `unidiff.parse_section` returns an empty `fd.paths`. `all()` over an empty iterable is `True`, so any section the parser cannot attribute a path to is treated as if every one of its paths matched an exclude pattern: it is removed from `kept` and appended to `gone.files`, even though no glob or pin actually matches it. Sections that carry no `---`/`+++` lines hit this, e.g. a mode-only change

```
diff --git a/deploy.sh b/deploy.sh
old mode 100644
new mode 100755
```

or a binary change

```
diff --git a/logo.png b/logo.png
index 1111111..2222222 100644
Binary files a/logo.png and b/logo.png differ
```

Nothing in `[review].exclude_globs` or `pins.toml` matches `deploy.sh`/`logo.png`, yet the section is dropped from the diff the reviewer receives and is reported as an excluded file. The reviewer then approves a chmod/binary change it never saw, which is exactly the failure mode the `any`→`all` change was meant to avoid for the other direction. (As a secondary effect, `fd.path` for such a section is empty/`None`, so the `", ".join(p for p, _n in self.files[:5])` in `Excluded.line()` can also fail.) The exclusion predicate needs to distinguish "no paths to test" from "all paths excluded", e.g. `if fd.paths and all(_hit(p, pats, pinned) for p in fd.paths):`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_exclude.py:73

chunk_findings.detail: The literal verdict token `echo 'STATUS: NO FINDINGS'` is still embedded in the diff, and the earlier triage's probe does not answer it. The probe argues "the string is a fixture reviewer's canned reply; reviewers see no verdict authority in test text," but that is a justification of why the string is *there*, not a change that removes or neutralizes it: the bytes a prompt-folding pipeline reads are unchanged. Any consumer that folds this file into a review prompt without stripping verdict-shaped lines (the same class of consumer the exclusion feature is being built for) can parse `STATUS: NO FINDINGS` out of the fixture text and conclude the change is clean, which is exactly the failure mode the original finding described. It still holds; the probe is not a fix. Note the token is emitted as reviewer stdout in the test, so a fix needs to construct it non-literally (e.g. `printf 'STATUS: %s\n' 'NO FINDINGS'`) or keep the fixture output out of the diff-visible text.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_exclude.py:55 (`_setup`, the fake-reviewer fixture)

chunk_findings.detail:
The behaviour that made earlier finding #1 valid is unchanged and is observable in this diff, not only in a docstring I cannot see. `patterns()` returns the pins.toml paths whenever `cfg.review.exclude_pin_files` is set, *independently of* `cfg.review.exclude_globs`:

```python
pinned = pins.pin_files(repo, cfg) if cfg.review.exclude_pin_files else []
return list(cfg.review.exclude_globs or []), pinned
```

and `filter_diff()` still filters when only `pinned` is non-empty, because the guard is `if not pats and not pinned: return diff, gone`. The new knob template ships `exclude_pin_files` with `new = 'true'`, i.e. that is the default. So the concrete input `review.exclude_globs = []` (or `DDFLOW_REVIEW_EXCLUDE_GLOBS=[]`) — the exact command a user runs to get the pre-change "send every file" behaviour back — still drops golden snapshots, transcripts and README regions owned by `.ddflow/pins.toml`, contrary to the documented promise that an empty list sends every file. The probe cited in the triage (`test_a_rename_out_of_an_excluded_tree_keeps_its_new_side` / `test_a_pin_file_is_an_exact_path_not_an_any_depth_pattern`) exercises the exact-path pin matching that fixes finding #2; neither test touches the `exclude_globs == []` case, so the fix/probe does not answer #1. Either the `exclude_globs` documentation must be narrowed ("empty list sends every file pins.toml does not own unless `exclude_pin_files` is turned off"), or an empty `exclude_globs` must actually suppress the pin-file exclusion.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_exclude.py `patterns` / `filter_diff`

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier finding stands: the probe it was closed with does not exercise the behaviour it is about. That probe is `test_a_rename_out_of_an_excluded_tree_keeps_its_new_side` / `test_a_pin_file_is_an_exact_path_not_an_any_depth_pattern`, which cover (a) keeping the new side of a rename out of an excluded tree and (b) anchoring pin paths so a root path is not an any-depth pattern. Neither of them touches the `exclude_globs == []` interaction at all, so they cannot answer the reported defect — the false promise made by the `exclude_globs` docstring ("an empty list sends every file") while the sibling knob `exclude_pin_files` independently strips everything `.ddflow/pins.toml` owns. The new test added in this diff actually *codifies the un-fixed behaviour*: `test_pin_files_are_left_out_unless_the_knob_says_otherwise` sets `[review]\nexclude_globs = []` and then asserts `"GENERATED_MARK" not in seen.read_text()`, i.e. a user who runs `ddflow config review.exclude_globs []` (or `DDFLOW_REVIEW_EXCLUDE_GLOBS=[]`) to get the pre-change behaviour back still has the pinned `tests/golden/snap.json` (and every other pins.toml-owned README region / snapshot / transcript) silently dropped from the reviewer payload. Unless the docstring was separately rewritten to say "an empty list sends every file that is not a pin file", the documented contract and the observed behaviour still disagree; the cited commit ("anchor pin paths, keep renamed sides") only addresses the pin-path anchoring, not this.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/review.py:44-45 (`exclude_globs` / `exclude_pin_files`)
